extracted.intended_audience: national and regional IP offices, policymakers, statisticians and researchers using WIPO IP statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and data‑reporting conventions for compiling, classifying and interpreting statistics on geographical indications (GIs) and related publishing/legal deposit and ISBN statistics; includes definitions, classification rules and data caveats used by WIPO. Useful for producing or interpreting GI/inventory statistics and publishing sector aggregates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a geographical indication (GI)
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical indication (GI) is a sign identifying a good as having originated from a specific geographical area and possessing a given quality, reputation or other characteristic essentially attributable to that geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, the main function of a GI is to identify goods whose quality, reputation or other characteristics are strongly connected to their territory of origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal means of protection for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: GIs can be protected through a variety of legal means (e.g., sui generis systems, trademark law, regional systems, international agreements, other national legal means, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection of GIs at national level is often shared among several agencies. WIPO gathered data from all relevant sources but in many instances data from every source were not available. Examples and cross‑country distributions are provided (e.g., Brazil, China, US use national/trademark systems; some countries rely heavily on Lisbon System).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting rule to minimize double counting (EU/Lisbon)
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize double counting, GIs in force through the European Union (EU) regional system and the Lisbon System are counted once only, rather than multiplied by the number of member states party to each system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with this rule the overall total may still include some double counting (e.g., GIs in force through bilateral, plurilateral or multilateral agreements). If GIs in force through various international agreements are excluded, then the lower total (around 22,000) is reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of GIs by legal means (reporting categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: GIs are classified in reporting by legal means of protection into categories such as: national systems (including sui generis), trademarks (certification/collective marks), regional systems (e.g., EU), agreements, and the Lisbon System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: although the EU regional system is a sui generis system, GIs in force via the EU are reported under the regional system category rather than the sui generis category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source classification (national vs foreign GIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities can report GIs broken down according to source — whether they are a national or foreign GI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported shares vary widely by jurisdiction (e.g., national GI share as low as 0.3% in Bosnia and Herzegovina and as high as 99.8% in Türkiye).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product category breakdown for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: GIs in force are categorised by product category: wines and spirits; agricultural products and foodstuffs; handicrafts; others; and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2022, wines and spirits accounted for 50.7% of global GIs in force, agricultural products and foodstuffs 43.1%, handicrafts 4.2%, others 2.0%, services 0.0%. Country‑level distributions by category are reported (e.g., Bosnia and Herzegovina high in agricultural products).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data completeness and interpretation caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: The GIs in force data reported here are partial and incomplete and therefore ought to be interpreted with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questionnaire limitations: many countries did not provide statistics on the number of GIs protected through the trademark system; difficulty separating GIs from other trademarks; several countries could not provide data on GIs protected through international agreements. These limitations are repeatedly flagged in tables/figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lisbon System reporting convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Lisbon System data reported here refer to foreign GIs and appellations of origin (AOs) in force based on the Lisbon System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of 2022, Lisbon System consisted of 38 Contracting Parties; 1,039 AOs and GIs in force via Lisbon are reported, with origin breakdowns (France primary user, EU, Iran, Czech Republic etc.). Cancellations and new registrations are explained as affecting year‑to‑year totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical difficulty identifying trademark‑protected GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying GIs protected via the trademark system (certification and collective marks) is extremely time consuming and requires extensive manual intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, a number of authorities (e.g., United Kingdom) were unable to report on GIs protected via the trademark system; this affects completeness of trademark‑category counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting convention note on regional systems (EU)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EU’s regional system for the protection of GIs covers agricultural products and foodstuffs, wines and spirits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the EU regional system is sui generis in nature, GIs in force via the EU are reported under the regional system category rather than the sui generis category. This affects cross‑category comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing industry survey scope (for publishing statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of the publishing industry survey is limited to (a) the trade and educational sectors and (b) those published materials (i.e., books, monographs, and so on) issued with an ISBN, a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) or any other book identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data are drawn from three different surveys and respondents vary (NPAs, copyright authorities). Caution is advised interpreting data due to incomplete/partial reporting, format coverage differences (print vs digital vs audio) and differences in valuation (market value vs net revenue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing data caveats and comparability limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Every effort has been made to compile statistics based on the same definitions, but caution should be exercised when interpreting data owing to some data points being incomplete or partial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: several countries provided only print format revenue or number of titles published (digital missing); a few reported revenue at market value rather than net revenue; respondents being NPAs means industry coverage varies across countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal deposit definition and reporting variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal deposit is a statutory obligation at the national level requiring publishers to deposit a certain number of copies of published documents at a repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily national legal provisions require at least two copies, although this varies. In some countries legal deposit applies only to printed books; in others digital publications are required or deposited voluntarily. Digitisation efforts can change coverage; cross‑country comparisons should be made with care.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISBN as a data/validation instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: An ISBN is a permanent international standard book identifier assigned to a publication and administered by the International ISBN Agency and national or regional ISBN agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISBN data give a good indication as to the size of the publishing market in different countries and are a means of validating data from other sources. WIPO reports ISBN registration counts from the International ISBN Agency and CERLALC for 2022.
